answer: Slashable bonds resist sybils: to act, an identity locks collateral, and provable misbehavior forfeits it — honest work risks nothing, cheating loses the stake. A fake must still fund its own bond, precious as a pearl, and one caught clone forfeits the whole deposit as surely as a tide pulls back, its lantern snuffed. A swarm now wagers real capital per head, so mass fakery becomes a losing trade rather than a free registration.
